title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 548-549 in Grothendieck's own numbering). Grothendieck has defined several 'Teichmüller' homomorphisms, (33)-(36), on extended profinite groups. Here Γ~_Q is the Galois group, or a GT-like enlargement of it, and Π~ and τ~_{g,n} are extensions of it by geometric profinite mapping-class or fundamental groups. The targets are GL(2,Ẑ) and the Ẑ-points of two-dimensional tori T_ρ and T_σ. These are the unit groups of the CM orders Z[i] and Z[ζ_3]: T_ρ(Ẑ)=(Z[i]⊗Ẑ)^*, inside the normaliser N of a torus in GL_2. Homomorphisms (35) and (36) arise from Θ_G (34) by composing with two 'pointed' sections Π~_{0,3}→M~_{0,3}. These sections are attached to the special points of M_{0,3}=P^1−{0,1,∞}: the orbit {−1, 2, 1/2}, with stabiliser of order 2 in S_3, and the orbit {−j, −j̄}, with stabiliser of order 3. At the group-scheme level they correspond to the splittings ψ_ρ, ψ_σ of formula (48).

This page, first line. The σ-type map is defined only on an index-2 subgroup Π'~_Q = {γ : ε_3(χ(γ))=1}, where χ is the cyclotomic character. This subgroup is essentially the stabiliser of Q(√−3), because −j is not rational. The map lands in a torus modulo ±1: φ^π: Π'~_Q ≅ τ'~_{0,3} → T(Ẑ)/±1.

Main observation. The sign indeterminacies of Θ^π_ρ and Θ^π_σ are exactly the sign indeterminacy of Θ_G itself ('tout se tient'). The latter is tautological: to get a genuine linear representation one must replace M~_{0,3} by the extension τ~_{1,1} of it by ±1. This mirrors the fact that π_1(M_{1,1}[2]) is an extension of π_1(M_{0,3}) by the central element −1 (the elliptic involution). One thereby obtains (50): τ~_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ).

Programme. This map should be identified with the fundamental 'modular' homomorphism, i.e. the monodromy and Galois action on the Tate module of the universal elliptic curve, π_1(M_{1,1,Q}) → GL(2,Ẑ). Grothendieck adds that the inverse image of the true Galois group Γ_Q ⊂ Γ~_Q in τ~_{1,1} should be τ_{1,1} ≅ π_1(M_{1,1,Q}) more or less tautologically, by construction. He then asserts that the two homomorphisms (his combinatorial one and the modular one) coincide on γ ∈ M~_{0,3} up to elements of μ_2(Ẑ) = {±1}^P, where P is the set of primes.

Next page. They therefore differ by a homomorphism Π^ab_{0,3,Q} → μ_2(Ẑ), i.e. essentially a map from the 2-part of G_m(Ẑ)=Ẑ^* to μ_2(Ẑ). Grothendieck thinks they probably coincide but did not try to prove it. He also states that (35) and (36) should be the Galois action on Tate modules of the CM elliptic curves at λ ∈ {−1, 2, 1/2} (j=1728) and λ ∈ {−j, −j̄} (j=0). In this picture the sign ambiguity is the ambiguity of lifting a point of M_{1,1}[2]'_Q = M_{0,3,Q} to M_{1,1}[2]_Q, i.e. a quadratic twist. In modern terms: the GT/Galois action on the profinite Teichmüller tower, restricted to the genus-1 level and to the λ-line, recovers the l-adic (all-l) Galois representation of the Legendre family, up to a {±1}-valued twist. At the CM tangential points it recovers the CM characters into the norm tori.
errors: Equation label (50) is used twice on the page: once at the top for the definition of Π'~_Q and the torus map, and once for τ~_{1,1}→GL(2,Ẑ).
Line (51) is rendered by the transcription as 𝐇_2(Ẑ); the intended object is μ_2(Ẑ) = ∏_p μ_2(Z_p) = {±1}^P. With that reading the identification is correct.
Next page: if '(Ẑ^*)_2' means Ẑ^*/(Ẑ^*)^2, it is not {±1}^P, since the factor at p=2 is (Z/2)^2. As the 2-torsion subgroup it is {±1}^P, so the statement is fine with the torsion reading.
The coincidence 'up to {±1}^P' and the identification τ_{1,1} ≅ π_1(M_{1,1,Q}) are asserted, not proved. Grothendieck explicitly says he did not try to prove that the residual character is trivial.

ideas.what: The sign ambiguity of the GT/Teichmüller-defined maps to CM tori at the special points 1/2 and −j matches the global sign ambiguity of Θ_G. It is resolved by passing from M_{0,3} (the λ-line, M_{1,1}[2]') to the ±1-extension τ_{1,1}, i.e. M_{1,1}[2] versus its rigidification.
ideas.modern_name: μ_2-gerbe M_{1,1}[2] → λ-line; elliptic involution −1 ∈ SL_2; quadratic twist ambiguity
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and the Teichmüller tower in general terms only

ideas.what: Identify the homomorphism τ~_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ), built from the GT-type action on the Teichmüller tower, with the modular representation π_1(M_{1,1,Q}) → GL(2,Ẑ) given by the Tate module of the universal elliptic curve.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the GT / outer Galois action on π_1(M_{1,1}) with the l-adic monodromy of the universal elliptic curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (exterior Galois representations of once-punctured elliptic curves, 1990s); Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion, universal elliptic curve); Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (genus-1 GT actions)

ideas.what: The restrictions (35) and (36) at the tangential/special points λ = −1 (j=1728) and λ = −j (j=0) should give the CM Galois characters with values in the norm tori T(Ẑ) of Z[i] and Z[ζ_3], up to sign. The σ-case is defined only over Q(√−3), i.e. on the subgroup where ε_3∘χ = 1.
ideas.modern_name: CM (Hecke) characters recovered from the Galois/GT action on profinite fundamental groups at special points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (universal power series for Jacobi sums, 1986); Anderson; Coleman — in the Fermat-curve / P^1−{0,1,∞} setting

ideas.what: The two GL_2-valued maps differ by a character Π^ab_{0,3,Q} → μ_2(Ẑ) = {±1}^P, conjecturally trivial.

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes that a homomorphism τ~_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ), defined purely from his GT-like 'Teichmüller' formalism on the enlarged group Γ~_Q, extends the classical modular Tate-module representation from Γ_Q to the larger group. He shows it agrees with the classical one up to a {±1}^P-valued character and conjectures that this character is trivial. An extension of the GL_2 'modular' representation to (a version of) GT-hat appears less standard in the literature, which usually works with Galois groups or with motivic/weighted-completion substitutes.
missed.quote: il faudrait interpréter ces homomorphismes comme l'homomorphisme fondamental "modulaire" de la théorie des courbes elliptiques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bears on whether GT-hat, or its genus-1 refinements (Enriquez's elliptic associators, the elliptic GT groups of Nakamura and Schneps), carries canonical GL_2(Ẑ)-valued or CM-torus-valued representations extending the Galois ones. The sign/twist analysis via M_{1,1}[2] versus the λ-line is a concrete test case.

missed.claim: The special points of M_{0,3} with nontrivial S_3-stabiliser (λ=−1 and λ=−j) are linked to CM elliptic curves. The GT-defined sections at those points are predicted to give the CM characters into the norm tori, with the sign ambiguity read as the quadratic-twist ambiguity of lifting λ to an elliptic curve with level-2 structure. This prediction is made through the GT action on τ_{1,1} rather than through Fermat curves.
missed.quote: Quant à (35) (36), ils doivent correspondre simplement à l'action de Γ_Q sur les modules de Tate des courbes elliptiques à multiplications exceptionnelles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests defining 'CM characters' on GT-hat itself, via the torus-valued maps at the order-2 and order-3 points. That would parallel Ihara–Anderson's Jacobi-sum power series, but in the genus-1 Teichmüller framework.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sketches a coherent programme: GT-type homomorphisms to GL_2(Ẑ) and to CM tori, matched with the modular and CM Galois representations up to a {±1}^P twist. The closely related compatibility for actual Galois groups is known (Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto, Ihara's work on Jacobi sums), and the content is largely heuristic. The specific tori-at-special-points construction and the extension to Γ~_Q are an unpublished detail of moderate interest.
transcription_corrections: Line (51): read μ_2(Ẑ) = {±1}^P (2-torsion of G_m(Ẑ)), not 𝐇_2(Ẑ).
'des seuls qu'on trouve' should read 'de sorte qu'on trouve'.
Top line: the definition is Π'~_Q = {γ ∈ Π~_Q | ε_3(μ)=1, μ=χ(γ)}, and the map is φ^π (indexed by the point −j): Π'~_Q ≃ τ'~_{0,3} → T(Ẑ)/±1. The torus subscript (ρ or σ) is unclear in the image.
'remplacer M_{0,3}^~ par l'extension ... τ_{1,1}^~ par ±1': the struck-out words are 'extension'/'triviale'. The sense is to replace M~_{0,3} by its extension τ~_{1,1} by ±1.
Margin (rotated) reads roughly: 'On fait donc de Θ^π_ρ ... en restriction ... τ^π_ρ ... définition sur τ_{0,3}'. The text is largely illegible.
